date_note: National Herald (published 23 November) says Smith spoke on Sunday; 22 November is that Sunday.
title: Microsoft's Brad Smith warns fast AI-driven patching could cause disruption in coming months
summary: According to National Herald India, Microsoft president Brad Smith told CBS's Face the Nation that AI has shortened the time needed to find code weaknesses and companies are patching "at a pace we have never seen before". He said rushed, under-tested patches, especially on older systems, risk new problems and the public should prepare for disruption in "the coming months". He said a recent outage "wasn't a cyberattack".
plain: Microsoft's president says companies are patching faster because AI finds flaws sooner, and that rushed updates may cause disruption. He said a recent outage was not a cyberattack.
exec: Microsoft's president says businesses should test updates more rigorously and replace ageing infrastructure.
action: Per Brad Smith as reported by National Herald: consumers should install security updates, and businesses should test updates more rigorously and replace ageing infrastructure.

validation.note: National Herald India and Infobae, two independent publishers, each report Brad Smith telling CBS Face the Nation that disruption may continue for months as organisations patch quickly. The CBS interview itself was not read.

review.note: Compared title, Sunday date, quotes, outage statement and advice against National Herald and Infobae
